title: Lacey Chabert recalls overnight Disney World filming
excerpt:
Holiday Ever After was filmed mostly overnight at Disney World.
The cast recalled fatigue and memorable sunrises.
body_md:
Lacey Chabert and her colleagues have shared their experiences of filming Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True, a Hallmark Christmas movie produced at Walt Disney World. Much of the production took place overnight, requiring the cast and crew to adjust their schedules while working in an environment normally associated with daytime entertainment.

Chabert, known for Mean Girls and her numerous Hallmark holiday films, plays Lindsey in the movie. The opportunity to work inside the theme parks was an appealing aspect of the production, but filming after regular operating hours also created practical challenges that differed considerably from the experience of visiting the parks as a guest.

The production needed to capture its material while the parks were closed to visitors. Its overnight schedule meant that the crew had a limited window in which to complete the necessary scenes before the parks returned to their normal daytime operations. That constraint placed additional importance on coordination and efficient use of the available filming hours.

Travis Van Winkle, who plays Philip, recalled that adjusting to the reversed working schedule took time. The performers had to remain alert and prepared for their scenes during hours when they would ordinarily be asleep. Even the novelty of working in a largely empty theme park could not entirely eliminate the fatigue associated with overnight production.

Bryce Durfee, who portrays Sam, and producer David Wulf compared the experience to living like vampires. Durfee acknowledged that staying awake could become genuinely difficult. Executive producer Jennifer Aspen also praised the performers for what they accomplished while adapting to the demanding schedule and the requirement to finish before daytime visitors arrived.

For Chabert, however, the unusual hours provided some particularly memorable experiences. She identified watching the sunrise inside Disney World as one of her favorite aspects of the night shoots. She also recalled preparing for work while the Magic Kingdom fireworks were taking place as the parks approached closing time.

Those moments offered the cast a perspective on the resort that most visitors rarely experience. The contrast between the festive atmosphere of the parks and the practical demands of overnight filmmaking became a distinctive part of the production's behind-the-scenes story.

Holiday Ever After is part of Hallmark's 2026 Christmas movie schedule. The retrieved report does not include an exact premiere date or the full wording of several interview quotations, so those details remain unspecified here.
